slides.title: Q3 2026 board update
slides.subtitle: Sample Co. · Board meeting · Sample data
slides.notes: Fictional company; all figures are sample data for testing.

slides.title: Q3 beat plan, but SMB churn puts year-end ARR $230k short; we propose moving two hires to onboarding
points: New business is healthy: Q3 new ARR beat plan by 21%, the third straight quarter above plan
SMB churn is now the binding constraint and puts year-end ARR about $230k short
The churn comes from SMB accounts that never finish setup, as onboarding load rose 41%
Moving two Q4 sales hires to onboarding attacks the cause and saves $110k a year
slides.notes: Lead with the ask; the rest of the deck is the proof.

slides.title: New ARR beat plan by 21% in Q3, the third straight quarter above plan

ghost.exhibit: bar — new ARR vs plan by quarter, Q1-Q3 2026, $k (actual highlighted)
evidence: E2 Plan new ARR Q1/Q2/Q3: $850k / $950k / $950k [SAMPLE]
E3 Q3 new ARR vs plan: +21% (Q1 +5.9%, Q2 +5.3%) [CALC]

slides.title: Ending ARR of $11.05M beat plan by 1.4%, a smaller margin than new ARR because churn rose

ghost.exhibit: table — Q3 ARR bridge: begin, new, expansion, contraction, churn, end vs plan, $k
evidence: E4 Q3 ARR bridge: begin $10,160k + new 1,150 + expansion 300 − contraction 80 − churn 480 = end $11,050k [SAMPLE]
E5 Q3 ending ARR vs plan $10,900k: +$150k, +1.4% [CALC]
E6 Q3 beat on new ARR ($200k) vs beat on ending ARR ($150k) [CALC]

slides.notes: New ARR beat plan by $200k, ending ARR by only $150k; churned ARR rose from $300k in Q2 to $480k in Q3.

slides.title: SMB churned ARR more than doubled since Q1 and now offsets a third of new bookings

ghost.exhibit: stacked bar — churned ARR by segment (SMB, mid-market), Q1-Q3 2026, $k
evidence: E7 SMB churned ARR Q1/Q2/Q3: $170k / $220k / $390k [SAMPLE]
E8 Mid-market churned ARR Q1/Q2/Q3: $70k / $80k / $90k [SAMPLE]
E9 Q3 SMB churned ARR as share of Q3 new ARR: 34% [CALC]

slides.notes: Mid-market churn is flat; the change is all SMB.

slides.title: If the SMB trend continues, year-end ARR lands about $230k below the $12.0M plan

ghost.exhibit: table — Q4 projection: Q3 end, new, expansion, contraction, churn, year-end vs plan, $k, with assumptions
evidence: E10 Q4 projected year-end ARR: $11,770k, $230k below $12,000k plan [CALC]
E11 Q4 new ARR, expansion, contraction equal Q3 (1,150 / 300 / 80) [ASSUMPTION]
E12 Q4 SMB churned ARR $560k; mid-market $90k [ASSUMPTION]

slides.notes: This is a projection on stated assumptions, not a forecast commitment.

slides.title: Most SMB accounts that churned in Q3 never finished setup in their first 30 days

ghost.exhibit: bar — Q3 churned SMB accounts by setup status (finished within 30 days vs not), count
evidence: E13 Q3 churned SMB accounts: 61, of which 44 (72%) never finished setup within 30 days [SAMPLE]

slides.title: Accounts that finish setup churn at about a fifth of the rate of those that do not

ghost.exhibit: bar — 90-day churn by setup status, Jan-Jun 2026 SMB cohort, %
evidence: E14 90-day churn, Jan-Jun 2026 SMB cohort: 4% if setup finished within 30 days, 19% if not (ratio 0.21) [SAMPLE]

slides.title: Setup completion fell from 68% to 55% as new accounts per specialist rose 41%

ghost.exhibit: line — setup completion within 30 days (%) and new accounts per specialist per month, Q1-Q3 2026
evidence: E15 Setup completed within 30 days: 68% / 61% / 55% (Q1-Q3) [SAMPLE]
E16 New SMB accounts per specialist per month: 42.5 / 50 / 60 (+41% Q1→Q3) [CALC]

slides.notes: Two specialists since January while monthly SMB sign-ups rose from 85 to 120.

slides.title: Shifting two Q4 sales hires to onboarding saves $110k a year and recovers about $82k of Q4 ARR

ghost.exhibit: two columns — plan as approved (4 AEs) vs proposed (2 AEs + 2 onboarding specialists): annual cost, Q4 ARR effect
evidence: E17 Annual cost: 2 AEs $300k vs 2 onboarding specialists $190k; saving $110k [CALC]
E18 At-risk backlog: 170 active SMB accounts not set up after 30 days; average SMB ARR $6.4k [SAMPLE]
E19 Q4 ARR recovered if half the backlog is set up: about $82k [CALC]
E20 New AEs need about 5 months to ramp, so Q4 hires add little Q4 bookings [ASSUMPTION]

slides.notes: The $82k is a rough estimate on stated assumptions (E19).

slides.title: The cost is slower sales capacity in 2027, which Sales has not yet sized

ghost.exhibit: two columns — what we give up (2 fewer AEs ramping into 2027) vs what we keep (Q4 bookings nearly unchanged)
evidence: E20 New AEs need about 5 months to ramp, so Q4 hires add little Q4 bookings [ASSUMPTION]
[DATA NEEDED] 2027 new-ARR capacity with 2 vs 4 Q4 AE hires, $k, from Sales capacity model; owner: VP Sales

slides.notes: Be explicit that this is open; commit to bring it to the January meeting.

slides.title: We ask the board to approve the swap and a revised year-end forecast of $11.85M

ghost.exhibit: three asks with owner and date
evidence: E10 Q4 projected year-end ARR: $11,770k, $230k below $12,000k plan [CALC]
E19 Q4 ARR recovered if half the backlog is set up: about $82k [CALC]
E21 Revised year-end ARR forecast $11.85M [CALC]
[DATA NEEDED] 2027 capacity model (see slide 11), due before January board; owner: VP Sales

slides.notes: Ask 1 approve requisition swap; ask 2 accept revised forecast; ask 3 review SMB churn and 2027 capacity in January.

slides.title: Cash runway stays near 22 months at the current $650k monthly burn

ghost.exhibit: table — cash, monthly net burn, runway
evidence: E22 Cash at end of Q3: $14.2M [SAMPLE]
E23 Net burn: about $650k a month [SAMPLE]
E24 Runway: about 22 months [CALC]

slides.notes: The swap lowers annual cost slightly; runway is not the constraint.
